item.title: Pagos cross-border: la nueva frontera de Koywe se dirige a Asia
item.description: Los pagos cross-border se han convertido en uno de los principales casos de uso del blockchain, con las stablecoins como un nuevo medio para mover dinero entre mercados y reducir algunas fricciones del sistema financiero tradicional. Bajo este modelo, la fintech chilena Koywe prepara su entrada a Asia en 2027. “Llevamos varios meses viajando con parte de nuestro equipo a ciertos países de Asia para acercarnos a los reguladores y a los abogados, y así entender cómo podemos hacer esto de la manera correcta”, aseguró Ignacio Detmer, cofundador y CEO de Koywe.

item.title: AIG Starts Parametric Cloud Outage Solution
item.description: American International Group (AIG) said it launched a new Parametric Cloud Outage Solution, providing clients an additional layer of cyber insurance protection to help them recover faster from business interruption losses resulting from cloud service outages and cloud provider downtime. AIG’s new Parametric Cloud Outage Solution triggers are based on a predefined formula that considers cloud service downtime and the associated potential financial impact. “AIG’s Parametric Cloud Outage Solution is designed to give organizations faster access to funds when disruptions occur, helping them respond with greater confidence and certainty while complementing their broader risk management and insurance programs.” AIG said spending on cloud infrastructure services has increased steadily among businesses of all sizes.

item.title: IDB arranges its first parametric catastrophe swap for Belize, Swiss Re backs it
item.description: The Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) has successfully arranged its first sovereign parametric catastrophe swap transaction, securing $20 million of hurricane risk transfer for Belize, underwritten by global reinsurance firm Swiss Re. In executing this catastrophe swap for Belize, the IDB has helped the country secure an almost two year source of parametric hurricane protection. The IDB said that its first successful catastrophe swap execution showcases “how countries can transfer disaster risks to international markets and access rapid liquidity following extreme events.” It forms part of the IDB’s broader work to help Belize enhance its resilience to natural disasters, building on $25 million of contingent financing already available to the country through the IDB’s Contingent Credit Facility for Natural Disaster Emergencies (CCF) and $118 million in approved loans protected by Climate Resilient Debt Clauses (CRDC), that allow for principal payments to be postponed in the event of a qualifying disaster.

item.title: Mangrove secures record catastrophe reinsurance cover for 2026 hurricane season
item.description: Mangrove Property Insurance Company, the Florida based specialist insurer, has secured a record-setting catastrophe reinsurance programme for the 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season, which is set to provide protection against both the frequency and severity of catastrophe events, with coverage reportedly extending to a 1-in-175 year storm. According to the announcement, Mangrove’s reinsurance programme also includes aggregate cover for protection against third and fourth events, as well as the placement of the firm’s debut $111 million Buttonwood Re Ltd. The Buttonwood Re 2026-1 cat bond provides Mangrove with capital markets-backed reinsurance protection on both a per-occurrence and annual aggregate basis covering losses arising from named storms across Florida.

item.title: Pillar Capital appoints Jessica Ferreira as Actuary
item.description: Pillar Capital Management Limited, the Bermuda-based specialist collateralized reinsurance and insurance-linked securities (ILS) investment manager, has appointed Jessica Ferreira as an Actuary. Pillar Capital had over US $4.3 billion in assets under management as of the second-half of 2025. Last October, we reported that Pillar Capital had promoted Kevin Ronaldson to the role of Chief Financial Officer (CFO) .

item.title: Pinion announces key additions to executive leadership and accounting team
item.description: Pinion Insurance, a London-headquartered specialty insurance carrier formed earlier this year, has announced three key additions to its executive leadership team and accounting function. Werner brings over two decades of industry experience to his hew position, joining Pinion in Chicago from Old Republic International, where he most recently served as Vice President, Chief Accounting Officer, Insurance Operations. In his role at Old Republic, he directed corporate insurance accounting operations, and manged corporate entities including internal reinsurance, and led the financial systems team.

item.title: PERILS decreases insured loss estimate for extratropical windstorm Nils to €695m
item.description: PERILS, a Zurich-based catastrophe insurance data provider, has disclosed a reduced loss estimate for extratropical windstorm Nils, also known as Ulrike, of EUR 695 million, which affected the Nouvelle-Aquitaine and Occitanie regions in southwest France from 11 to 13 February 2026. This is the third industry loss estimate for the extratropical windstorm, and compares to the previous loss estimates of EUR 586 million and EUR 767 million issued by PERILS six weeks and three months after the event end date, respectively. Luzi Hitz, Product Manager, PERILS, commented, “The European windstorm season 2025/26 witnessed two events which fall under our PERILS CORE coverage: Goretti in January 2026, which we currently estimate at EUR 479 million, and Nils in February, currently estimated at EUR 695 million.

item.title: Orbital Sentry secures new capital to bring continuous satellite monitoring for wildfire risk
item.description: With the newly secured capital, Orbital Sentry can move into its next phase of growth, specifically by helping to accelerate the development of continuous satellite monitoring for wildfire risk and national security applications. By delivering continuous, high-sensitivity infrared tracking, Orbital Sentry aims to overcome the constraints of legacy systems that rely on intermittent “point in time” data and fail to match the pace of world events. Orbital Sentry, a deep-tech startup building persistent infrared imaging systems for geosynchronous orbit (GEO), has announced the close of a pre-seed funding round led by Ridgeline, with participation from Superorganism and Hustle Fund.

item.title: Liechtenstein Rules Out Paying Hackers’ Ransom After Data Breach
item.description: Late last month hackers penetrated Liechtenstein’s confidential registry of foundations and trusts, accessing data on the names and residencies of the beneficial owners of some 31,000 entities registered in the country. Two weeks after an unprecedented hacking attack shook the tiny Alpine principality of Liechtenstein and its outsize financial center, officials say they still don’t know who the perpetrators were or what they want. Yet one thing is clear according to its prime minister: the country won’t pay a ransom for the data.

item.title: Belgian Firefighters Battle Record Blaze Near German Border
item.description: Emergency services were attempting to control a large wildfire in the east of Belgium on Sunday, after the blaze destroyed about 2,700 hectares (6,700 acres) of a nature reserve and forced about 600 residents to evacuate in an area near the German border. The fast-moving wildfire is nearing the German border, with the city of Monschau , a major tourist hub in the Eifel region, in focus. Local authorities early Sunday morning urged residents in parts of the town to evacuate to prevent health risks from smoke, though they later said that for now there’s no reason to believe that the fire will spread into German territory.

item.title: SEC to Keep Hands Off Shareholder Proposals, Worrying Activists
item.description: financial regulator on Friday made permanent its decision to cease judging whether companies may exclude shareholder resolutions from votes at annual meetings, leaving investor activists concerned about diminishing influence. Securities and Exchange Commission extends a freeze put in place last November on deciding whether to approve corporate requests to skip votes on shareholder proposals. It said it has created an “extensive body of guidance” about whether shareholder proposals could be excluded or not.

item.title: HSBC UK partners with Gallagher to expand business insurance support
item.description: “By referring customers to Gallagher’s specialist teams, we’re helping businesses get the right insurance advice and risk management support quickly and conveniently,” said Jon Barks, head of business risk UK CMB at HSBC. The partnership gives HSBC UK’s commercial banking customers another route to specialist insurance support, while expanding Gallagher’s reach through the bank’s established business customer network. HSBC UK has partnered with Gallagher to provide specialist insurance services to its commercial banking customers, giving businesses access to insurance advice, risk management support and insurance products through the broker.

item.title: Gallagher partners with HSBC UK
item.description: Gallagher announced a new affinity partnership with HSBC UK to provide insurance services to the bank’s commercial banking clients. Under the arrangement, businesses with insurance requirements will be referred to Gallagher for insurance advice, risk management support and access to insurance products. HSBC UK serves ~600k business and commercial clients.

item.title: Amazon’s New User Agreement Seeks to Curb Class-Action Suits
item.description: reintroduced a clause in its user agreement that seeks to prevent shoppers from filing class-action lawsuits against the online retailer, inserting a legal buffer between itself and plaintiffs attorneys that it removed five years ago. Plaintiffs attorneys could still seek class-action lawsuits against Amazon, and it would be up to a judge to determine if the user agreement prevents them from doing so. In an email sent to customers on Friday, the company said a new “arbitration agreement and class-action waiver” will require shoppers to resolve disputes outside the courts but said they could still file small claims, cases that typically limit damages to a few thousand dollars.

item.title: Report Says Firefighting Tactics at Maine Lumber Mill Inadvertently Aided Deadly Blast
item.description: Firefighters who responded to a fire at a Maine lumber mill used tactics that inadvertently contributed to a massive explosion that killed three people, according to a report from federal investigators. The fire companies tried to extinguish the May 15 fire inside a silo at the Robbins Lumber mill in rural Searsmont, Maine, by injecting it with water — unaware of warnings from the manufacturer that doing so would be dangerous. “The application of water into the silo in this incident likely entrained oxygen into the silo headspace, stirred up dust within the contents, and caused it to become suspended in an explosive concentration.” The report recommends that fire departments make sure firefighters choose appropriate tactics for silo fires and never direct water or foam into oxygen-limiting silos.

item.title: Britain Considers Easing 2030 Zero-Emission Vehicle Targets
item.description: Britain on Friday set out a range of options that could ease the pressure on car manufacturers to switch new sales to zero-emission vehicles, launching a review of the existing targets which gradually phase out new petrol and diesel cars. The mandate, introduced in 2024, requires carmakers to ensure a rising proportion of their annual sales are zero-emission vehicles, with EVs accounting for 33% of new car sales in 2026, 80% in 2030 and 100% by 2035. Related: Carmakers Broadly Win Round One in Massive UK Suits Over Diesel Emissions The policy is designed to accelerate the industry’s transition to electric vehicles by imposing fines on manufacturers that miss the targets.

ABIR Chair Mark Cloutier said: “On behalf of the board of the Association of Bermuda Insurers and Reinsurers, I wish to welcome the new members of the Finance Committee. ABIR said the new Finance Committee members will support the association’s ongoing work on financial and industry matters affecting Bermuda’s insurance and reinsurance market.

item.title: A Challenged Man Took the Fall for a Crash But Amended Complaint Came Too Late
item.description: The plaintiffs also cannot expect to prevail if an amended complaint—naming a different driver—is substantially different from the initial lawsuit and was filed years later, a Florida appeals court said this week in a case that involved a Tampa bowling alley, a 2014 crash that killed a 27-year-old, and court proceedings that were complicated by the COVID-19 pandemic and lost evidence. By the time the amended complaint was filed, critical evidence had been lost and at least one key witness had died. “Because Sillaway and Edgerton’s amended complaint necessarily predicated Brandon Crossroads’s liability on a brand-new factual narrative, the trial court did not err in concluding that the amended complaint did not relate back,” the appellate panel concluded .

item.title: US Ready to ‘Take Any Actions Necessary’ to Fight EU ESG Rules
item.description: The Trump administration “will take any actions necessary to address unreasonable burdens on US commerce” if the European Union doesn’t rein in its ESG regulations, according to a letter addressed to the EU by the US government. The US is doubling down on its efforts to quash European environmental and human rights rules it says unfairly impact American companies. The comments were accompanied by a post on X by US ambassador to the EU, Andrew Puzder, who said “it’s time for the EU to deliver” on what he described as an earlier commitment by the bloc to ensure American companies won’t face “undue restrictions” on trade.

item.title: FTC Probes Health Records Giant Epic Systems, Sources Say
item.description: Epic Systems, a healthcare database company that holds the medical records of hundreds of millions of Americans, is facing an antitrust investigation by the U.S. Epic runs the patient web portal MyChart along with other electronic health record systems. The FTC has sent investigative demands to others in the health technology industry seeking information about how Verona, Wisconsin-based Epic grants or withholds data access, the sources said.

item.title: Training the People Behind the Claims Assessments: Allstate Claims University
item.description: Late last week, Allstate unveiled Allstate Claims University, a 33,000 square foot campus in Dallas, complete with hands-on property and auto labs—immersive training environments representing scenarios that claims professionals will face in the real world. In a statement about the opening of the campus, Mike Fiato, executive vice president and chief claims officer at Allstate, said, “The investment in Allstate Claims University starts with our people and ends with our customers.” “When someone’s home is damaged by a storm or their vehicle is involved in an accident, they need more than a claim processed: they need an expert who can understand what happened, explain what comes next and help them move forward.” “By investing in our teams, we’re helping ensure customers receive the expertise, care and confidence they need when it matters most,” Fiato said. “The investment in Allstate Claims University starts with our people and ends with our customers.” Allstate reported that the company has 23,000 claims professionals supporting roughly 8.5 million claims each year.

item.title: FactorLab Turns Workplace Language into Risk Signals
item.description: FactorLab sees a possible analogue in commercial workplace risk. (Image credit: IIR/Gemini.) Commercial insurers have long relied on inspections, documentation and loss history to understand how effectively an insured manages workplace risk. FactorLab (Pleasanton, Calif.) believes another potentially valuable source of risk information has largely gone untapped: what workers and supervisors actually say while preparing to do the work.

item.title: Blenheim launches Knot-on-Time
item.description: Blenheim Partnerships, part of White Bear Group, has launched Knot-on-Time, an insurance solution protecting vessel owners against losses caused by the delayed delivery or non-delivery of newly built ships. The product was developed and is led by Edward Parker, senior underwriter for special risks at Blenheim Partnerships. The coverage can address higher vessel-replacement costs, lost charter income, financing expenses, contractual liabilities and mitigation costs associated with securing alternative tonnage or commissioning a replacement vessel.

item.title: SafetyCulture rebrands as Mitti
item.description: Australian workplace operations platform SafetyCulture has rebranded as Mitti , marking what the Australian company calls the biggest transformation in its history. In 2020, SafetyCulture and QBE launched Mitti Insurance , a joint venture combining small business insurance with virtual risk assessments and workplace-safety tools. Now, SafetyCulture has become Mitti, while SafetyCulture Care has returned to the Mitti Insurance name.

item.title: Hawaii Faces Rare Hurricane Strike as Storms Batter Indiana
item.description: Hawaii is in line for a rare hurricane strike as Tropical Storm Lala grazes the Big Island, while severe storms threaten more flooding and outages across Indiana. This would be the first hurricane strike anywhere in Hawaii since Iniki in 1992. Related: Hawaii Faces More Tropical Threats From El Niño-Charged Pacific In the Midwest, nearly 200,000 homes and businesses are without power across Indiana after days of severe weather disrupted air travel and caused widespread flooding and damage.

item.title: Hackers Claim Mass Data Theft From Shell, Philips, GE, Fiserv And Dozens of Others
item.description: A prolific hacking group known for exploiting software vulnerabilities to attack multiple targets simultaneously claimed it had stolen large volumes of data from nearly 50 companies worldwide, including Philips, Shell, Fiserv and GE, according to a posting on the group’s website. Philips said it had been targeted by Cl0p while Shell said it was aware of a recent “possible incident,” confirming an earlier report on Thursday by Dutch media outlet BNR. “Philips has identified and contained an attempted cybersecurity compromise of a specific enterprise server related to internal data,” Philips said in a statement, adding that the incident does not impact customer environments.

item.title: Driving Above the Speed Limit Costs You, Doesn’t Save Much Time
item.description: More than 43% of the studied trips included at least one instance of speeding, and drivers spent nearly 12% of their driving time going faster than the speed limit. They found that if drivers of light-duty, conventional internal combustion engine vehicles actually drove at posted speed limits, it could save an average of $22 million, based on fuel costs at the time, 6.7 million gallons of fuel, and 57,000 metric tonnes of carbon dioxide every day. If your objective is to get to your destination safely and to save fuel, then you might drive slower than the speed limit,” said William Northrop, mechanical engineering professor at the University of Minnesota and study co-author.
